language.script_notes: Rioplatense Spanish as national, but with a strong ongoing Andean/Indigenous (Quechua/Aymara-influenced) cultural presence reflected in place names and local vocabulary.
false_friends: Bolivia (shares the same Andean altiplano/puna landscape just across the border)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Present on winding mountain routes; often absent on high-altitude unpaved roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: As national, though many roads are unpaved at higher altitude.
road_furniture.curb_style: Cobbled streets in colonial Andean villages (Purmamarca, Humahuaca).
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; roads climbing dramatic switchbacks are common given the terrain.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs on traditional adobe houses, suited to the arid climate.
architecture.roof_material: Flat adobe/mud roofing traditional; some corrugated metal in larger towns.
architecture.wall_construction: Flat-roofed adobe construction — thick mud-brick walls that blend into the landscape — is the defining regional architectural signature; colonial Spanish churches and cobbled streets in towns like Salta city.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Earthy adobe tones matching the surrounding desert and colourful mountain strata; whitewashed colonial church facades in town centers.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Flat-roofed adobe village houses (Purmamarca, Humahuaca); colonial Spanish churches; salt-flat and altiplano infrastructure; llama/alpaca corrals.

nature.vegetation: Sparse high-altitude puna desert vegetation — hardy shrubs, cacti, tough grasses; almost no trees at the highest elevations.
nature.terrain: Dramatic multicoloured mountain strata (the Quebrada de Humahuaca's 'Hill of Seven Colours'), high-altitude salt flats (salinas), and the Andean altiplano/puna plateau bordering Bolivia and Chile.
nature.climate_signature: High-altitude arid desert — intense sun, dramatic colour in the exposed rock strata, thin cold air; visually the most vividly colourful landscape in Argentina.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4WD vehicles more common given high-altitude unpaved mountain roads; llamas/alpacas frequently visible alongside roads rather than motor vehicles in the most remote areas.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 3 and Gen 4 near Salta city; increasingly sparse and older at higher altitude.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage concentrated on the main tourist routes (Salta–Purmamarca–Humahuaca); genuine gaps at the highest, most remote altiplano elevations.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the same Andean altiplano/puna landscape, similar adobe architecture and Indigenous cultural presence right across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Argentine plates and Rioplatense Spanish phrasing differ from Bolivian plates and Bolivia's stronger day-to-day Quechua/Aymara bilingual signage; Argentina's national road furniture (chevron markers, Mercosur-style plates) is absent in Bolivia.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar high-altitude Andean terrain, adobe architecture and llama/alpaca herding culture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's plates, signage and road furniture differ entirely from Argentina's; Peru also sits much further north with different vegetation zones despite superficial altiplano similarity.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script and plate style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The northwest is colourful high-altitude desert with adobe villages; the Pampas is flat green farmland, and Patagonia is dry windswept steppe — visually distinct from both.
